## Moon Valley in Chile: a private half-day excursion

**Moon Valley is one of the most striking places to discover the landscapes of the Atacama Desert.** Dry rocky ridges, salt deposits and sandy expanses create unusual scenery whose colours change throughout the day.

Ada Tours departs from the [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) area. This **half-day** excursion is private and includes [Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/), the entrance fee and a cocktail.

The trip suits travellers who want to discover Atacama's landforms without a long hike. The exact short walks, transport and departure time must nevertheless be agreed for the chosen day.

## Why is the valley compared with the Moon's surface?

The terrain of the Cordillera de la Sal was shaped by rock formations, salt and wind erosion. Dry air and almost complete lack of vegetation in many areas emphasise the contours of the ridges and slopes. Some dunes and rock outcrops are particularly striking.

The name Moon Valley comes from its appearance: sharp lines, dry basins and exposed rock suggest another world. It is a visual comparison, not the site of an extraterrestrial impact, and this terrestrial landscape has its own geological history.

On a walk, notice the texture of the slopes, salt at the surface and changing colours as the sun moves. A place that looks pale in the morning can turn reddish towards evening. Photographs are especially interesting when low light brings out the relief, but access to particular viewpoints depends on the area's current regulations.

## Los Flamencos Reserve and visiting rules

[Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/) forms part of [Los Flamencos National Reserve](/chile/place/los-flamencos-national-reserve/) in the Antofagasta Region. Conservation rules and the participation of local communities guide how the area is managed. CONAF's official page explains visitor routes, opening hours and the requirement to follow staff and guides' instructions.

Stay on authorised paths and viewpoints. In such a dry environment, natural surfaces recover slowly, and stepping off a path can damage fragile ground or lead into hazardous areas.

Do not assume conditions from other parts of the reserve apply to Moon Valley: lagoons, salt flats and mountain sectors have their own visiting arrangements. Admission to Moon Valley is included in this excursion, but that does not mean access to every other sector of Los Flamencos.

## What does the cocktail format offer?

A **cocktail** is included in our excursion. This is a confirmed element of the experience, although the exact drink, serving location and any snacks are not publicly specified.

Timing is also important. Many travellers hope to see Atacama in evening light, when the rock formations become especially vivid. On this route, sunset is **possible only if the schedule allows**. If a flight or long transfer follows, time in Moon Valley must be coordinated with it.

| Part of the programme | What is confirmed |
|---|---|
| Destination | Moon Valley near San Pedro |
| Duration | Half a day |
| Format | Private excursion |
| Services | Entrance fee and cocktail |

When choosing the trip, explain in advance how important evening light is to you and whether you have any essential connections that day. The organiser can then assess whether the valley can realistically be visited at the desired time.

## Weather, altitude and what to bring

Atacama is known for strong sunlight, dry air and substantial temperature differences between day and evening. Wear closed comfortable shoes, a hat and sunscreen; bring water and clothes that can be layered.

Routes at higher altitudes also depart from San Pedro, with different acclimatisation requirements. Moon Valley should not automatically be equated with high-altitude lagoons or geyser fields. When planning several excursions, take account of the actual altitude, exertion and transfers involved in each one.

Find other nature journeys in our [Wildlife and Nature catalogue](/interests/wildlife/) or read about [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/).

## Frequently asked questions about Moon Valley

### How long does the excursion last?

The published itinerary lasts **half a day**. The exact departure time depends on the selected day and any onward travel.

### Is the entrance ticket included?

Yes. The entrance fee is included in our excursion.

### Is the excursion always at sunset?

No. Sunset is possible only when the schedule allows, for example when a subsequent flight does not require an earlier return.

### What does 'cocktail' mean in the programme?

A cocktail is listed as an included part of the excursion. The published terms do not specify the exact drink or additional snacks.

## Tours with a Moon Valley excursion: what's included and how the route works

[Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/) lies near [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) in northern Chile. The rocks of the Cordillera de la Sal, sandy dunes and salt formations look particularly striking in low sunlight. The area provides an introduction to desert scenery without a multi-day trek.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with the standalone [Moon Valley with a Cocktail excursion](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/chile-moon-valley-cocktail-half-day/). When comparing options, examine how long the visit lasts, what is included and any subsequent transfers, because the excursion occupies only part of a multi-day journey.

## Half a day in Atacama: admission, cocktail and sunset

This excursion takes **half a day**, with the entrance fee and a cocktail included. The route passes through rocky valleys in the area of [Los Flamencos Reserve](/chile/place/los-flamencos-national-reserve/). Views of the Andes and changing light add to the desert experience.

Atacama's sunset colours are appealing, but the programme has an important qualification: **watching the sunset is possible only if the subsequent flight schedule permits it**. If travellers continue to another region on the same day, the excursion must be timed around their flight. A long evening stop cannot be promised for every departure schedule.

Bring water, a hat, sunglasses, skin protection and comfortable closed shoes for the dry desert. These are recommendations for preparation, not items provided as included services.

## Example: Moon Valley on a 17-day Grand Tour

On the [17-day Chile, Argentina and Brazil Grand Tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/), travellers arrive in San Pedro de Atacama from Santiago via Calama Airport. The following day, **day 7**, begins with a half-day Moon Valley excursion. The journey then continues by private aircraft to Punta Arenas, with an onward helicopter connection towards Puerto Natales.

The excursion day's price includes admission and a cocktail. The timing of the excursion, flight and subsequent helicopter transfer is agreed before booking, including whether sunset can be seen. The day therefore combines a nature experience with substantial travel logistics. Those wishing to spend several evenings in the desert should compare the number of overnight stays separately.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_chile_argentina_private_grand_tour_17_days}}

The wider programme also covers [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/), Chilean Patagonia, Mendoza, Iguazu Falls and Buenos Aires. Moon Valley is an important but short section of the journey. If Atacama is your main interest, compare [other Chile tours](/chile/tour/) with more stops in the north.

## Choosing a trip that includes this excursion

Compare the actual day-by-day itineraries: is there a night in San Pedro before the excursion, how much time follows it, and is an immediate flight planned? A journey with a flight on the same day lets you see the desert within an extensive itinerary. A trip with several days in San Pedro may better suit those who want to add other confirmed visits to the region.

We help coordinate the excursion and transport sequence within the chosen itinerary. The specific time, conditions and possible changes are checked against the offer before booking.

## Frequently asked questions about tours featuring Moon Valley

### How long does the cocktail excursion take?

It lasts half a day. The full journey's duration depends on the selected tour: in the 17-day route above, a flight to Patagonia follows.

### Are Moon Valley admission and the cocktail charged separately?

Both are listed as included in [this excursion](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/chile-moon-valley-cocktail-half-day/). Other services depend on the chosen multi-day tour.

### Can a sunset visit be guaranteed?

No. On a tour with a flight the same day, a sunset stop depends on the agreed transport schedule.

### Is this a good route for exploring Atacama in depth?

It is suitable for a first introduction to Moon Valley within a larger journey. For a more detailed exploration, compare itineraries through [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) by their number of days and included excursions.

## Excursions from San Pedro de Atacama: what to choose

[San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) is a small oasis in northern Chile and a convenient base for salt flats, volcanoes and high-altitude lagoons. The scenery changes over a few hours: the dry salt formations of Moon Valley, pools frequented by flamingos and the starry night sky all call for different excursions and preparation.

Our excursions vary in more than the places visited. There are private half-day programmes, full-day group tours and evening telescope sessions. It is easier to decide **which part of Atacama you want to discover** first, and then choose the duration and conditions.

## Moon Valley: rocks and evening light

[Moon Valley with a Cocktail](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/chile-moon-valley-cocktail-half-day/) is a private **half-day** programme. Admission and a cocktail are included. The route explores the dry rock landscapes of the Cordillera de la Sal and [Moon Valley](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/).

The valley is known for salt and rock formations: ridges, dunes and places that change colour in low sunlight. However, **sunset is not guaranteed** for every itinerary, because it depends on the schedule. This is a suitable first look at the desert without a long trip into the highlands.

## High-altitude lagoons and flamingos

[Atacama: High-Altitude Lagoons, Socaire and Toconao](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/atacama-highland-lagoons-socaire-toconao-full-day/) is a **full-day group excursion**. You visit [Miscanti](/chile/place/laguna-miscanti/) and [Miñiques](/chile/place/laguna-miniques/), have lunch in [Socaire](/chile/place/socaire/) and continue to [Chaxa Lagoon](/chile/place/laguna-chaxa/), where flamingos can be observed at the salt flat. The final stop is [Toconao](/chile/place/toconao/) with its church and bell tower.

**Lunch at Socaire and lagoon admission tickets are included** in our excursion. It is a full day with significant changes of altitude; temperatures by the lakes may be much colder than in San Pedro.

## Astronomy excursions

Atacama nights are known for low artificial light levels and dry air. We offer an [Evening with Professional Telescopes](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/atacama-astronomy-telescope-evening/) lasting **1.5–2 hours**. Our other [night-time astronomy excursion](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/chile-atacama-astronomy-tour/) is described as group observation with an English-speaking guide; see its own page for conditions and dates.

Stargazing depends on weather, the lunar phase and sky visibility. Even in the desert's favourable climate, clouds and a bright Moon can change the programme. If astronomy is the main reason for your trip, leave an extra evening free.

## El Tatio geysers: a separate early departure

The [El Tatio Geysers](/chile/place/el-tatio-geysers/) lie at a higher altitude than the town, so excursions often set off before sunrise. We offer different routes, including a [dawn excursion with breakfast and a thermal pool](/chile/el-tatio-geysers/el-tatio-dawn-breakfast-thermal-pool/) and a [trip via Machuca](/chile/el-tatio-geysers/el-tatio-machuca-standard-half-day/).

Because of the altitude and cold, this is a different type of excursion from an evening Moon Valley visit. Consider how you feel before departure, dress warmly and do not approach hot water beyond permitted barriers.

## Comparing excursions

| Destination | Format |
|---|---|
| Moon Valley | Private, half-day |
| Lagoons and Chaxa | Group, full day |
| Telescopes | Evening, 1.5–2 hours |
| El Tatio | Early departure |

Over **2–3 days** in San Pedro, you could spread your experiences across one desert outing, one high-altitude excursion and an evening of stargazing. This is a planning example, not a promise of a fixed Ada Tours package. With only one day available, choose between a half-day introduction to the landscape and a longer lagoon excursion.

## Practical preparation

The nearest major airport is El Loa at Calama; Chile's official tourism agency gives a distance of approximately **100 km** from there to San Pedro. Hot days and cold nights call for layered clothing, water, sunglasses and comfortable shoes. After arrival, allow time to acclimatise before more demanding high-altitude journeys.

Reserves and desert sectors may have separate admission and advance-booking rules. When purchasing an excursion, check which tickets are included in that specific programme.

## Frequently asked questions about San Pedro excursions

### Can you combine Moon Valley and stargazing?

These are separate half-day and evening excursions. Combining them depends on when the daytime outing ends and whether an evening programme is available.

### Do all excursions have Russian-speaking guides?

There is no general promise of that. Individual pages specify English-speaking guidance and group or private formats; choose the language for each particular excursion.

### Are admission tickets to the high-altitude lagoons included?

Yes, they are included in our [Miscanti–Miñiques–Chaxa group programme](/chile/san-pedro-de-atacama/atacama-highland-lagoons-socaire-toconao-full-day/) along with lunch in Socaire.

## An excursion to San Rafael Glacier in Chilean Patagonia

[San Rafael Glacier](/chile/place/san-rafael-glacier/) descends into the lagoon of the same name in northern Chilean Patagonia. A boat travels among icebergs, with a tall ice front and blue crevasses ahead. It suits travellers who want to see a Patagonian glacier **from the water**, without promises of landing on the ice or walking across its surface.

The glacier is part of Laguna San Rafael National Park. CONAF, the park authority, describes several ways to reach the area, including a route from [Puerto Río Tranquilo](/chile/place/puerto-rio-tranquilo/) through Exploradores Valley.

## How the Ada Tours excursion works

We offer a [San Rafael Glacier via Exploradores Valley excursion](/chile/puerto-rio-tranquilo/san-rafael-exploradores-boat-full-day/). This is a **full-day programme**, approximately **08:00–18:00**.

The journey starts with a drive through [Exploradores Valley](/chile/place/exploradores-valley/) to [Exploradores Bay](/chile/place/exploradores-bay/). Travellers board a boat and continue by water towards San Rafael Lagoon. From the route, you can see the ice wall and floating ice. The return journey leads back to Puerto Río Tranquilo.

The trip has two distinct sections: the drive and navigation on the lagoon. Time spent on the water depends on travelling conditions and the captain's decisions. The exact distance of approach to the glacier cannot be promised: the crew must account for icebergs, wind and water conditions.

## What you see from the boat

The main attraction is the glacier front rising steeply above the water. Ice may appear almost white or a vivid blue, with icebergs of different sizes drifting nearby. Pieces occasionally break from the ice wall, but **calving cannot be guaranteed according to a schedule**, and approaching too closely is dangerous.

The boat trip reveals the glacier's size differently from a photograph taken ashore. The lagoon changes constantly as ice and wind move, so the scenery on a particular day will differ from promotional photographs.

## San Rafael versus Exploradores Glacier

The names appear together in this region, but they refer to **different glaciers**. On our route, [Exploradores Valley](/chile/place/exploradores-valley/) serves as the overland approach to the boat trip on San Rafael Lagoon.

An official CONAF notice from 2026 specifically warns that **access onto Exploradores Glacier is prohibited because of unstable ice and risks to visitors**. Do not confuse this restriction with tourist boating to San Rafael. If you see an old Exploradores walking itinerary online, verify whether it remains valid directly with the park authority.

## Choosing a glacier excursion

| Question | This route |
|---|---|
| Starting point | Puerto Río Tranquilo area |
| Duration | Approximately 08:00–18:00 |
| Main experience | Boat and glacier |
| Walking on ice | Not stated |

A single fixed price and detailed list of included services have not yet been confirmed for our excursion. When planning, check which transfers, meals and park tickets are included in the quote for the chosen date. This is especially important in a remote part of Patagonia, where transport and weather shape the journey.

## What to bring

Conditions around the lagoon can be wet and windy. Even in summer, a waterproof windproof jacket, warm layers, a hat and camera protection will be useful. Follow crew instructions on board: standing or moving freely to the edge during manoeuvres can be dangerous.

## Frequently asked questions about San Rafael Glacier

### Can you see San Rafael in one day?

We offer **a full-day excursion** with an early departure and a return in the late afternoon. Whether it can operate on a particular date depends on navigation and road conditions.

### Can the boat approach right up to the ice wall?

There is no such promise. The crew chooses a safe distance based on floating ice and water conditions.

### Is walking on the ice included?

No. Our excursion provides **a boat trip to San Rafael**, not a walk on the glacier.

## Excursions to Santa Lucía Hill in Santiago

[Santa Lucía Hill](/chile/place/santa-lucia-hill/) stands in the centre of Santiago. Stairs and paths cross its slopes among trees, fountains and historic architectural features. The upper viewpoints offer views over the capital, while at the foot of the hill **Neptune Terrace** is particularly well known for its monumental fountain.

It is a convenient sightseeing stop: after walking city streets, visitors see Santiago from above and discover the history of this city park. The time available for the climb depends on the excursion's duration and which sections are open.

## Which Ada Tours excursions include Santa Lucía?

We offer two different formats for discovering central Santiago:

- [Santiago: Historic Centre and Eastern Neighbourhoods](/chile/santiago-de-chile/santiago-private-historic-centre-east/). The route connects [Plaza de Armas](/chile/place/santiago-plaza-de-armas/), historic city buildings, [La Moneda](/chile/place/la-moneda-palace/) and Santa Lucía Hill with modern eastern districts. The excursion's start time is coordinated with arrival and check-in.
- [Santiago: Historic Centre and Modern Neighbourhoods in a Group](/chile/santiago-de-chile/santiago-historic-east-russian-group/). This **group programme includes a Russian-speaking guide**; after visiting central landmarks, the route continues to Vitacura, Las Condes and Providencia.

Both versions introduce Santa Lucía, but they are not the same excursion. The second explicitly specifies a group format and Russian-language guiding. The first places greater emphasis on the visiting sequence and arranging the start time; Russian-speaking guidance should not be assumed to be guaranteed.

## What to see on the hill itself

Neptune Terrace features fountains and architectural details recalling the 19th and 20th centuries. Higher up, stairs lead to shaded spaces, monuments and viewpoints. The city's tourism authority notes that the modern park took shape following improvements begun in 1872 under Benjamín Vicuña Mackenna; the hill was declared a historic monument in 1983.

The park is also known for Hidalgo Castle and several terraces. A longer independent walk can be arranged, but an excursion that also includes La Moneda and eastern neighbourhoods **does not promise to cover every attraction on the hill**.

## Combining Santa Lucía with the historic centre

| Stop | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Santa Lucía | Hill and city panorama |
| [Plaza de Armas](/chile/place/santiago-plaza-de-armas/) | Main square |
| [La Moneda](/chile/place/la-moneda-palace/) | Government palace |
| Eastern neighbourhoods | Modern Santiago |

The route illustrates the capital's development from its colonial core to newer city districts. Architecture enthusiasts may prefer to devote more time to the older streets; an introductory tour across several neighbourhoods suits a first visit.

## Preparing for the walk

The hill has many steps and stone surfaces. Wear shoes suitable for climbing, and consider the needs of anyone who finds stairs difficult. The city park is generally open to the public, but particular sections may close for operational reasons. According to the municipal tourism service, **the park closes in rainy weather**. Check current opening rules on the city's official website for your chosen date.

You can visit independently by going straight to the historic centre. If the hill is part of a longer excursion, confirm the length of the stop: it may not be enough for a complete independent walk.

## Frequently asked questions about Santa Lucía Hill

### Can you climb the hill during a sightseeing excursion in Santiago?

Yes, Santa Lucía features in both our sightseeing programmes. The extent of the walk depends on the schedule and park accessibility.

### Is there a group excursion with a Russian-speaking guide?

Yes. The [group tour of the centre and eastern neighbourhoods](/chile/santiago-de-chile/santiago-historic-east-russian-group/) explicitly includes Russian-speaking guidance.

### Is the park open when it rains?

The municipal tourism portal reports that the park closes in rainy weather. Check current visiting conditions before departure.
